subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Which owner should claim canonical `openai` auto session route-state cleanup for doctor: the OpenAI plugin, the Codex doctor contract, or a provider-agnostic auto-fallback repair in core?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but `openai` is the canonical OpenAI provider id and Codex tests already preserve explicit canonical OpenAI sessions, so the permanent owner boundary should be chosen before automation changes provider ownership.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add an OpenAI doctor contract for `providerIds: ["openai"]` or equivalent OpenAI-owned route-state metadata, and keep Codex ownership limited to legacy Codex ids and runtime pins.

options.title: Codex also claims openai
options.body: Add `openai` to Codex sessionRouteStateOwners as the smallest repair, accepting the need for careful tests so normal OpenAI user/runtime pins are not misclassified.

options.title: Core owns auto-fallback cleanup
options.body: Move this specific `modelOverrideSource: "auto"` stale-fallback cleanup into a provider-agnostic core doctor path, which is cleaner for fallback semantics but a broader change.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add an OpenAI doctor contract for `providerIds: ["openai"]` or equivalent OpenAI-owned route-state metadata, and keep Codex ownership limited to legacy Codex ids and runtime pins.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged doctor session route-state owner and repair framework and the adjacent providerless Codex session override repair.
